title: A directed colimit of affine formal algebraic spaces glued by closed immersions is affine
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a directed system of affine formal algebraic spaces whose transition maps are closed immersions inducing isomorphisms on reductions, the colimit is an affine formal algebraic space (statement lines 7867-7874). The proof reorganises the system so that it becomes a colimit of affine schemes over a single directed set: each member of the original system is written as a colimit of affine schemes over its own directed set with thickenings as transition maps, and for every stage of a member and every later member one chooses a stage of the later member through which the corresponding morphism factors, which is possible by the factorisation statement for morphisms from quasi-compact objects into a colimit (proof lines 7876-7885). The morphisms so obtained are closed immersions inducing isomorphisms on reductions, hence thickenings (proof lines 7885-7887). Taking the disjoint union of the index sets with the order generated by factorisation makes a directed set, and the colimit of the original system is rewritten as the colimit of all the affine stages over it, which is the required presentation of the colimit as a filtered colimit of affine schemes with thickenings as transition maps (proof lines 7887-7900). The claim is H2: the argument is a reindexing, but each of its steps -- the choice of compatible stages, the identification of the induced morphisms as thickenings, and the verification that the new index set is directed and computes the same colimit -- is carried out explicitly.
